description: Random init baseline; also prints the public attributes of the task object.
Window attention + AND-gate keyword neurons + priority attention (decision list); default ENTY.
Decision list with bigger head-noun gazetteers; bare 'what is X' means DESC, 'what is the' means ENTY.
Adds an ENTY head-noun tier so the earliest noun wins, plus how-did/does DESC and person-name rules.
Adds agent-noun suffix detectors (-ist, -ician, -ographer, -ress) as HUM plus broad category nouns.
Adds wildcard gap patterns: a short 'what is X' (ends by position 20) means DESC; '^name' means HUM.
Adds small semantic noun groups for each class seen in dev errors (office-holders, facts, odds, etc.).
Merges plural/singular nouns into stems and prunes error-specific one-off words to cut dev overfitting.
EPS=30: one priority tier trades off against 10 characters, so early keywords can beat later higher tiers.
EPS=8: milder position trade-off, one priority tier is worth about 37 characters.
EPS back to 3; 'come from' outranks '^where'; bare '^which' defaults to HUM like '^name'.
Ablation: reverts '^which', removes the agent-noun suffix detectors to measure what they contribute.
Fixes stacked salience: one unanchored where/why at tier 8 instead of duplicate keywords firing together.
Replaces one-hot letters with a 5-bit code and +/-1 AND weights; same matches with far fewer parameters.
Tightens the short-question test by four characters so the attention window shrinks from 24 to 20 heads.
Tests whether past-tense 'what was/were/did' questions without a head noun lean DESC instead of ENTY.
Ablation: reverts past-tense DESC and removes the 'of what' ENTY rule.
Ablation: removes the small tier-5 DESC noun group (nature, function, facts, information, ...).
Ablation: restores the DESC nouns and removes the '^name' HUM rule.
Same model as e18 plus a dev-only diagnostic that lists keyword neurons firing on zero or one questions.
Collapses all how-adjective keywords into one 'how'=NUM neuron (verbs override to DESC); prunes dead neurons.
Prunes the 55 keyword neurons that fire on only one dev question to measure the long tail's value.
Restores the e20 keywords; drops '^what is the'=ENTY so those questions default to DESC.
e20 rules with BETA=2, EPS=0: decision attention becomes a soft vote over keywords instead of a hard list.
Restores the hard decision list; GAMMA=5 tests whether the position kernel can use smaller weights.
GAMMA=10: looks for the sharpness threshold below which long AND patterns start losing activation.
Adds past-tense agent verbs (invented, wrote, won, ...) as a general HUM signal at tier 4.5.
Removes agent verbs; default class HUM instead of ENTY for questions where no keyword fires.
Default back to ENTY; drops the redundant 'what do you call' so the attention window shrinks to 18 heads.
Merges tiers 5.2 and 5.5 into 5 to test whether those fractional priorities matter.
Moves 'come from' from tier 8.5 to tier 9, removing another fractional priority.
All priorities become integers: 'how' moves to tier 5 and the 'what is the' group moves to tier 4.
Divides the decision attention weights by three (BETA=100, EPS=1), keeping the same ratio.
Adds a question-final 'do' detector: questions ending in 'do' ask for a description (DESC).
Fixes e33, whose pattern had a stray space and never fired: 'do' followed directly by padding means DESC.
Same model as e34 plus a dev-only table of question-final words by class, to find useful endings.
Removes the dead 'do' rule and adds 'in the world' as a LOC signal at tier 5.
Removes 'in the world'; EPS=0 tests whether the earliest-keyword tie-break is needed at all.
Restores the tie-break; tightens the short-question test from position 16 to position 14.
Removes the short-question rule and the pad channel entirely; the window shrinks to 16 heads.
Shortens the two longest keywords ('you say', 'expectancy') so the window shrinks to 15 heads.
Removes the unused suffix and wildcard compiler paths; stem forms shrink the window to 14 heads.
All attention heads share one key projection (p, p^2) instead of keeping separate identical copies.
Ablation: drops the '^what does a/an/the' and '^what are some' ENTY overrides.
Restores the 'what does a' overrides; removes rare near-duplicates (stands for, comes from, whom, what 's a).
Restores the near-duplicates; every keyword casts a plain vote of 1 instead of a priority-scaled vote.
GAMMA=8: narrows the sharpness threshold, which lies between 5 (fails) and 10 (works).
GAMMA back to 10 for margin; BETA=20, EPS=0.2 tests how soft the decision attention can get.
Sanity check: EPS=-1 flips the tie-break so the latest keyword wins instead of the earliest.
Final: integer-tier keyword decision list with 5-bit letters, 14 window heads, shared key, earliest keyword wins.
